Houston, if you watched Ricardo O’Farrill’s 2026 YouTube special *Corto Circuito*, you know he doesn’t dodge the hard stuff.

O’Farrill has been doing stand-up since 2011. He brings a sharp Mexican point of view, sarcasm, and stories that turn personal chaos into real laughs. His recent special draws from addiction, rehab, mental health, and sobriety. If you like comedy with a point of view and no soft edges, I’d see this one.

Houston, Gauri B is set to headline the NYC South Asian Comedy Festival this October.

Her comedy is dark, personal, and satirical, with stories about gender, race, power, and the odd rules we all live by. She grew up in Punjab, and her live sets make room for crowd work, too. I’d catch this one if you like jokes with a point and a little bite.

Houston, you may know Winston Hodges from Netflix’s *Funny AF with Kevin Hart*.

He’s got a conversational style and doesn’t dodge the hard stuff—grief, growing up Southern, politics, religion. His 2020 YouTube special, *Grieving Productively*, shows why that honesty lands. Live, he likes to work the crowd and follow the room. I’d see this one in person.

Houston, you may know Sophie Hunter from AP Studio Files, where she talked music, writing, TikTok, and her sense of humor.

Her Linktree calls it “ctrl_alt+pop+rap.” Expect sharp flow, raw storytelling, and the kind of confidence that works better in a room than on a screen. I’d go if you like artists who say it straight.
